n: The heading mentions Jeduthun, a temple musician. David’s soul waits in silence for God alone; his rescue comes only from him. The Hebrew word “only” or “truly” repeats six times in this psalm.

f.g: Hebrew ʾak — “only, surely,” a keyword of this psalm.

n: God alone is his rock, salvation and fortress, so he won’t be badly shaken.
David turns to his attackers: how long will you gang up on one man? You are like a leaning wall or a fence about to collapse.
Their only goal is to topple him from his high position. They speak blessings outwardly but curse inside.

f.w: they bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly

n: He coaches his own soul: be silent and wait for God alone; your hope comes from him.
The refrain of verse 2 returns, now stronger: not just “not greatly moved” but “not moved” at all.
His salvation and honor rest on God, his mighty rock and refuge.
He invites everyone to trust God always and pour out their hearts to him. God is a safe place for all of us.

f.w: pour out your heart before him

n: Humans — whether lowly or important — are just a breath. On a balance scale, they weigh less than air.

f.w: to be laid in the balance

n: Don’t trust in force or stolen goods. Even if wealth grows honestly, don’t set your heart on it.

f.w: if riches increase, set not your heart upon them

n: A Hebrew way of saying “I’m certain”: God spoke once, and I heard it twice — power belongs to God.

f.w: God hath spoken once; twice have I heard this

n: Not only power but loyal love belongs to God. He repays everyone according to what they have done.

f.w: thou renderest to every man according to his work
